title: warcraft-learner spec rulebook
description: AI-generated rulebook for a single WoW specialization. Extract all major offensive cooldowns, all personal defensive cooldowns, and the spec's checkable rotation/cooldown usage rules from the supplied guide content. Output ONLY the raw JSON object - no markdown fences, no preamble. The first character must be '{' and the last must be '}'.

spec.description: WCL spec name, e.g. SubtletyRogue. Must match the spec being analysed.

spec_icon.description: Required. The spec's zamimg icon file stem (no extension), e.g. 'ability_stealth'. Read it from the spec's guide page; it becomes the spec's dropdown art. Must be set on every rulebook.

major_cooldowns.description: REQUIRED and must be populated. All major cooldowns: abilities with a cooldown >= 30s that meaningfully affect damage output (or healing/tanking if applicable). Include on-use trinkets when the guide mentions specific timing for them. Every spec has at least one major cooldown; a spec with an empty list produces no burst/rotation bench, so this must contain at least one item.

defensives.description: REQUIRED and must be populated. Every personal defensive cooldown with a cooldown >= 15s: immunities, absorb shields, significant damage reductions (>= 20%), and meaningful self-heals. Do NOT include passive talents or stance toggles.

rules.description: High-signal rotation and cooldown usage rules that are CHECKABLE against the player's log: cast timing, buff and debuff uptime, resources spent at a cast, enemies engaged, and cooldown usage against top parses. Every rule needs a condition, so omit anything that cannot be expressed as one - guidance the engine cannot judge is not a rule. Quality over count: a spec with two real rules is better than one with eight, and an empty list is valid.

source_summary.description: 2-3 sentences summarising the cooldown strategy these guides recommend.

guide_count.description: Added automatically by the admin CLI on save - do not populate manually.

saved_at.description: Added automatically by the admin CLI on save - do not populate manually.

name.description: Exact ability name as it appears in-game.

spell_id.description: WoW spell ID - REQUIRED. Prioritize the Active Ability Cast ID rather than a passive Aura, Classic WoW ID, or Talent Node ID. Verify at wowhead.com/spell=<id>. If genuinely unsure, supply your best guess and record the uncertainty in id_note - NEVER in usage_rule, which is shown to users as coaching copy.

duration.description: Optional. Active buff/window duration in seconds.

align_with_bloodlust.description: true if the guide explicitly says to sync this with Bloodlust / Heroism / Time Warp. Default false if the guide does not mention it.

opener_priority.description: Optional. Cast order in the opener (1 = first). Only set if the guide specifies a sequence.

usage_rule.description: One sentence: when and how to use this cooldown.

id_note.description: Optional. Internal maintainer note for any spell-ID uncertainty (e.g. 'best guess for the Midnight X cast, verify on Wowhead'). NEVER shown to users and not read by any analysis - put verification/best-guess notes here instead of in usage_rule.

talent_gated.description: Optional. Set to true when this ability requires a specific talent that not all builds take. When true, having zero casts is treated as normal rather than a 'never used' error.

spell_id.description: WoW spell ID - REQUIRED, same rule as major_cooldowns.

usage_rule.description: One sentence: when/why to press this button.

id_note.description: Optional. Internal maintainer note for any spell-ID uncertainty (e.g. 'best guess for the Midnight X cast, verify on Wowhead'). NEVER shown to users and not read by any analysis - put verification/best-guess notes here instead of in usage_rule.

talent_gated.description: Optional. Set to true when this ability requires a specific talent that not all builds take.

type.description: Rule category. cooldown_pairing: two abilities must be cast together or in sequence. cd_hold: an ability should be delayed until an anchor cooldown is available. opener: specific sequence or timing required at pull. rotation: ongoing priority or combo maintained throughout the fight. aoe_switch: behavior changes when multiple targets are present.

priority.description: critical (fundamentally breaks the spec if ignored), high (major DPS loss), medium (moderate optimization), low (minor min-maxing).

description.description: Short rule title shown in the UI (<= 60 chars).

condition.description: REQUIRED machine-readable trigger. Every rule is judged against the player's recorded behaviour, so a rule that cannot be expressed as one of the kinds below does not belong in the rulebook. Pick the kind that matches what the rule actually says rather than bending it into a cast-timing proxy: a rule about a buff being up wants castOutsideBuff or auraUptimeBelow, a resource threshold wants resourceAtCast, and a target count wants castAtTargetCount.

action.description: Second-person prescriptive instruction. Must tell the player what to DO, not describe what the rule checks. Good: 'Always cast Secret Technique within 5s of Shadow Dance.' Bad: 'Shadow Dance was cast without Secret Technique beforehand.'

castWithoutPrior.description: Flag each cast of spell_id that is not accompanied by required_spell_id within window_s seconds, on the side given by position.

spell_id.description: The spell being judged. Every cast of it is either a pass or a violation.

required_spell_id.description: The companion spell that must accompany spell_id. Under the default position 'before' it must already have been cast, so the ability that comes FIRST goes here and the ability being judged goes in spell_id.

window_s.description: Seconds within which the required spell must appear, measured from the judged cast.

position.description: Where required_spell_id must sit relative to the judged cast. 'before' (the default) requires it to come first, which is what most rules mean. 'after' requires it to follow. 'either' accepts both sides - use it only when the rule text genuinely says pair or sync rather than naming an order.

exception.description: Optional. Exempt casts that occur within a specific context window (e.g. during a major 2-minute cooldown window).

holdCooldownForAnchor.description: Flag casts of spell_ids that land within hold_window_s seconds before a non-opener cast of anchor_spell_id.

spell_ids.description: Spells that should be held for the anchor.

anchor_spell_id.description: The anchor cooldown the spells should be saved for.

hold_window_s.description: Seconds before the anchor cast within which the held spells are flagged.

castOutsideBuff.description: Judge each cast of spell_id against whether the buff was actually up, read from applybuff/removebuff. Prefer this over castWithoutPrior whenever the rule names a buff rather than a companion cast: 'inside Metamorphosis' means the aura, and a cast-to-cast proximity window only approximates it.

spell_id.description: The spell being judged. Every cast of it is either a pass or a violation.

buff_spell_id.description: The aura whose active spans decide each cast.

require.description: 'inside' flags casts made while the buff is down, for rules reading 'only during X'. 'outside' flags casts made while it is up, for rules reading 'never during X'.

auraUptimeBelow.description: Flag when the aura's total uptime across the fight falls under min_pct. Use for the 'keep X up' family, including damage-over-time effects the player maintains on the boss.

min_pct.description: Uptime percentage the player is expected to hold, taken from the guide rather than rounded to 100.

on.description: 'self' for a buff on the player. 'target' for a debuff the player maintains on enemies, which is how most damage-over-time rules are written.

openingSequence.description: Flag an opener whose first casts do not contain the given spells in the given order, within window_s of the pull. Extra casts between them are allowed, so list only the spells whose order actually matters.

spell_ids.description: The opener spells, in the order they must be cast.

window_s.description: Seconds from the first cast of the pull within which the sequence must complete.

cooldownUnderused.description: Flag when the player got meaningfully fewer casts of spell_id than the benched top parses did on this encounter. Use for the 'keep X on cooldown' and 'do not sit on X' family. The expectation comes from the bench, so the rule states no number of its own; spell_id must be one of the spec's major_cooldowns or it has no benchmark.

castAtTargetCount.description: Flag casts of spell_id made at the wrong number of engaged enemies, counted from the distinct targets the player damaged around the cast. Set min_targets for an ability that is only worth pressing on several targets, max_targets for a single-target ability that should give way to a cleave. At least one bound is required.

min_targets.description: Casts made at fewer enemies than this are violations.

max_targets.description: Casts made at more enemies than this are violations.

resourceAtCast.description: Flag casts of spell_id made at the wrong resource level, read from the resource snapshot on the cast. Set min_amount for a spender that should only go off at a threshold, max_amount for a generator that should not be pressed near the cap. At least one bound is required; an overcap rule is a generator with max_amount just under the cap.

resource_type.description: WCL power type id for the resource, e.g. 4 for combo points.

resource_name.description: Resource name for the finding copy, e.g. 'combo points'.

min_amount.description: Casts made below this are violations.

max_amount.description: Casts made above this are violations.

procWasted.description: Flag each span of buff_spell_id that ended without any of the spend spells being cast during it. Use for procs the rotation is supposed to consume on sight.

spend_spell_ids.description: Any one of these cast during the span counts as consuming the proc.
